questions.prompt: Some people believe that university education should be free for every student, funded entirely by the government. Others argue that students who benefit from it should pay for it themselves. To what extent do you agree or disagree that higher education should be free at the point of use?

Some argue that artificial intelligence will create more jobs than it destroys, while others predict widespread unemployment as machines take over skilled work. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
An increasing number of companies allow their employees to work entirely from home. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this development for both employers and workers?

Individual action on climate change, such as recycling and reducing personal energy use, is often described as meaningless compared with the emissions of large industries. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
Traffic congestion in major cities has reached levels that damage both the economy and public health. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could governments take to address it?
Social media platforms should be held legally responsible for false information published by their users. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Some people think governments should tax unhealthy food and drink to improve public health. Others believe this unfairly penalises the poor and that diet is a matter of personal choice. Discuss both sides and state your position.
Examinations are an inadequate way of measuring what a student has actually learned, and continuous assessment should replace them. How far do you agree with this view?
English has become the dominant language of international business, science and academia. What are the benefits and drawbacks of one language occupying this position?
In many developed countries, people are choosing to have children later in life or not at all. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects will it have on society?
Children under the age of sixteen should be banned from owning smartphones. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

Some believe that governments should fund the arts, including museums, theatres and orchestras, from public money. Others argue that such money is better spent on essential services. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Plastic waste in the world's oceans continues to increase despite decades of public awareness campaigns. Why has progress been so slow, and what practical solutions would be most effective?
A four-day working week with no reduction in pay would make employees more productive rather than less. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Many schools now teach coding and digital literacy from the earliest years, sometimes at the expense of subjects such as history or art. Is this a positive development, and what should a modern school curriculum prioritise?
International tourism has grown rapidly over the past fifty years. What are the advantages and disadvantages of mass tourism for the countries that receive large numbers of visitors?
Prison sentences should focus on rehabilitating offenders rather than punishing them. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this approach to criminal justice?

Some people argue that public money should fund space exploration because of the knowledge and technology it produces. Others say those funds are urgently needed on Earth. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Rates of anxiety and depression among young adults have risen sharply in recent decades. What do you think are the main causes of this increase, and what are its consequences?
Governments should provide every citizen with a guaranteed basic income regardless of whether they work. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Studying at a university in a foreign country is increasingly common. What are the benefits and the difficulties of pursuing higher education abroad?
Nuclear power is the only realistic way to meet the world's energy needs without worsening climate change. How far do you agree with this claim?

Some believe that traditional newspapers and broadcast journalism remain essential to democracy. Others argue that online sources have made them obsolete. Discuss both positions and state which you find more convincing.
Housing has become unaffordable for young people in many of the world's largest cities. What are the causes of this crisis, and what can governments realistically do about it?
Employers should be permitted to consider an applicant's social media activity when making hiring decisions. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Personal data is now collected by almost every service people use online. Who should control that data, and how far should governments go in regulating its use?
Many countries are introducing telemedicine, allowing patients to consult doctors remotely by video. What are the advantages and disadvantages of delivering healthcare in this way?
Museums should return historical artefacts to the countries from which they were originally taken. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many species of animal and plant life are disappearing at an unprecedented rate. What are the principal causes of this loss of biodiversity, and what will its effects be?

Some educators argue that homework is essential for reinforcing learning, while others believe it places unnecessary stress on children and their families. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Voting in national elections should be compulsory for all eligible citizens. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this idea?
Self-driving vehicles are expected to become common on public roads within the next two decades. What are the potential benefits and risks of this development?
Many employees report feeling burnt out and unable to disconnect from work outside office hours. What are the causes of this problem, and what steps could employers and governments take to solve it?
Advertising aimed at children should be prohibited entirely. How far do you agree with this position?

Some argue that free trade agreements raise living standards in every country involved. Others believe they mainly benefit large corporations at the expense of local workers. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Universities are increasingly judged by the salaries their graduates earn. Is this a reasonable measure of educational success, and what else should be taken into account?
Physical education should be compulsory at every stage of schooling, including the final examination years. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Levels of trust in politicians and public institutions have fallen in many countries. What has caused this decline, and what consequences does it have for society?
Some governments are restricting private cars from city centres altogether. What are the advantages and disadvantages of car-free urban centres?
The convenience of online shopping has done more harm than good to local communities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Some people believe widespread video surveillance in public places makes cities safer. Others regard it as an unacceptable intrusion on privacy. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Fresh water is becoming scarce in many regions of the world. What are the main reasons for this shortage, and what measures could be taken to manage water more sustainably?
Globalisation is gradually erasing the differences between national cultures, and this is a loss for humanity. How far do you agree with this statement?
Automation is expected to eliminate many routine jobs over the coming decades. How should governments prepare their workforce for this change, and who should bear the cost of retraining?
Learning a second language should be compulsory in primary school rather than beginning in the teenage years. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many countries are experiencing significant immigration. What are the benefits and the challenges of large-scale migration for the receiving country?

Some believe that healthcare should be funded entirely through taxation and free to all. Others argue that a private system delivers better quality and shorter waiting times. Discuss both views and state your position.
People increasingly encounter news only from sources that reflect their existing beliefs. Why is this happening, and what effects does it have on public debate?
Wealthy nations have a greater obligation than developing ones to reduce carbon emissions. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many students now use artificial intelligence tools to help write essays and complete assignments. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this for education?
Loneliness is now described by some researchers as a public health crisis, particularly among the elderly. What are the causes of increasing social isolation, and how might communities address it?
The enormous salaries paid to professional athletes cannot be justified when compared with those of teachers, nurses and other essential workers. How far do you agree?
Multinational companies often pay very little tax in the countries where they earn their revenue. Why does this happen, and what should be done about it?
Some argue that vocational training deserves the same status and funding as academic degrees. Others maintain that universities must remain the priority. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Companies should be legally required to publish the pay of every role they advertise. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this requirement?
Young people in many countries are leaving rural areas for large cities. What are the reasons behind this migration, and what effects does it have on the places they leave behind?
Streaming services have replaced cinemas and broadcast television for many viewers. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this shift for audiences and for the film industry?
Governments should invest far more in preventing illness than in treating it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Cybercrime is costing individuals and businesses increasing amounts of money each year. What are the main reasons for its growth, and what can be done to reduce it?

Some people believe that the elderly should be cared for by their families at home. Others think this responsibility belongs to the state and professional carers. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: School uniforms
questions.prompt: Many schools require pupils to wear a uniform, arguing that it reduces visible differences in wealth and improves discipline. Critics say it suppresses individuality and adds an unnecessary cost for families. To what extent do you agree or disagree that school uniforms should be compulsory?

questions.subject: Single-sex schooling
questions.prompt: Some parents believe that children learn more effectively in single-sex schools, where they face fewer distractions and less pressure to conform to gender stereotypes. Others argue that mixed schools prepare young people better for adult life. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Home education
questions.prompt: A growing number of parents are choosing to educate their children at home rather than sending them to school, often citing concerns about class sizes, bullying or the curriculum. What are the advantages and disadvantages of homeschooling for the children concerned?

questions.subject: Ban on smacking children
questions.prompt: Several countries have made it illegal for parents to smack their children, even lightly, as a form of discipline. Others regard this as an unwarranted intrusion by the state into family life. To what extent do you agree or disagree that physical punishment by parents should be banned?

questions.subject: Teacher shortages
questions.prompt: Many countries are struggling to recruit and retain enough qualified teachers, particularly in subjects such as mathematics and science, and many new teachers leave the profession within a few years. What are the causes of this shortage, and what measures could be taken to solve it?

questions.subject: Childhood obesity
questions.prompt: The proportion of children who are overweight or obese has increased considerably in many parts of the world over the past few decades. What are the main causes of this trend, and what effects is it likely to have on individuals and on society?

questions.subject: Grouping pupils by ability
questions.prompt: Many secondary schools divide pupils into classes according to their academic ability. Supporters claim this allows teaching to be pitched at the right level, while opponents argue it labels children and limits their progress. To what extent do you agree or disagree with grouping students by ability?

questions.subject: Starting age for formal schooling
questions.prompt: In some countries children begin formal lessons in reading and arithmetic at the age of four, while in others they do not start until seven. Some people believe an early start gives children an advantage, whereas others think young children learn best through play. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Gap year before university
questions.prompt: Many school leavers choose to spend a year travelling, volunteering or working before they begin university, while others move straight from school into higher education. What are the advantages and disadvantages of taking a gap year?

questions.subject: Compulsory financial education
questions.prompt: Many young adults leave school without understanding how to budget, borrow responsibly or save for the future. Financial education should therefore be a compulsory subject in every secondary school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Grandparents as childcare providers
questions.prompt: In many families grandparents now provide regular childcare while both parents work. What are the effects of this arrangement on children and on the grandparents themselves, and should governments offer any form of support for it?

questions.subject: Bullying in schools
questions.prompt: Bullying remains a serious problem in schools, and with the spread of social media it increasingly follows children home. What are the causes of bullying among young people, and what can schools and parents do to reduce it?

questions.subject: Performance-related pay for teachers
questions.prompt: Some governments have proposed that teachers' salaries should be linked to the examination results achieved by their students, in the same way that bonuses reward performance in other professions. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Decline in outdoor play
questions.prompt: Children today spend far less time playing outdoors without adult supervision than previous generations did, and far more time indoors in organised activities or in front of screens. What are the reasons for this change, and what effects does it have on children's development?

questions.subject: Fully online degrees
questions.prompt: It is now possible to complete an entire university degree online without ever attending a campus, and many institutions are expanding the courses they offer in this format. What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying for a degree in this way?

questions.subject: Competition in school sport
questions.prompt: Some people believe that school sport should emphasise competition, teaching children how to win and lose. Others argue that it should focus on participation and enjoyment so that no child is discouraged from exercising. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Abolishing private schools
questions.prompt: Private schools allow wealthy families to buy educational advantages for their children, including smaller classes and better facilities. They should therefore be abolished so that all children attend state schools. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: University dropout rates
questions.prompt: A significant proportion of students who begin a university degree leave before completing it, often with considerable debt and nothing to show for it. What are the main causes of this problem, and what could universities and governments do to address it?

questions.subject: Voting at sixteen
questions.prompt: Young people aged sixteen and seventeen can work, pay taxes and in some countries marry, yet they are not permitted to vote. The voting age should therefore be lowered to sixteen. How far do you agree with this view?

questions.subject: Decline in reading for pleasure
questions.prompt: Fewer children and teenagers now read books for enjoyment in their free time than in the past, even though books have never been cheaper or easier to obtain. What are the causes of this decline, and what effects might it have on young people and on society?

questions.subject: Part-time jobs for teenagers
questions.prompt: Many secondary school students take part-time jobs in shops, cafes or restaurants while they are still studying, sometimes working several evenings a week. What are the advantages and disadvantages of teenagers working during their school years?

questions.subject: Moral education at home or school
questions.prompt: Some people believe that teaching children right from wrong is primarily the responsibility of parents. Others argue that schools should play the leading role in developing children's values and character. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: School league tables
questions.prompt: Publishing official league tables that rank every school by its examination results helps parents make informed choices about their children's education and pushes weaker schools to improve. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

questions.subject: Paying children for chores
questions.prompt: Some parents pay their children for helping with household tasks such as cleaning and cooking, while others believe such tasks are simply part of family life. Should children be rewarded with money for doing chores, and what does each approach teach them?

questions.subject: Youth unemployment
questions.prompt: In many countries young people are far more likely to be unemployed than older workers, even when they hold good qualifications, and a slow start can affect their earnings for years. What are the causes of high youth unemployment, and what measures could be taken to reduce it?

questions.subject: Sharing children's images online
questions.prompt: Parents regularly post photographs and details of their children's lives on social media without the children's consent. The law should restrict how much parents are allowed to share about their children online. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Boarding schools
questions.prompt: In some countries it is common for children to attend boarding schools, living away from their families for most of the year and returning home only during the holidays. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this form of education?

questions.subject: Classic versus contemporary literature
questions.prompt: Some educators believe that school literature courses should focus on established classics that have shaped the culture. Others argue that contemporary works which reflect students' own lives are more engaging and relevant. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Grade inflation
questions.prompt: In many education systems the proportion of students receiving the highest grades has risen steadily over several decades. What are the causes of this grade inflation, and what effects does it have on students, employers and universities?

questions.subject: Compulsory community service for youth
questions.prompt: All young people should be required to complete a year of community or national service after leaving school, working in areas such as care, conservation or emergency services. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this idea?

questions.subject: Rural and urban school gap
questions.prompt: Children who attend schools in rural areas often achieve lower results than those in cities, and have fewer opportunities to continue their education. What are the causes of this gap, and what could be done to close it?

questions.subject: Private after-school tutoring
questions.prompt: The widespread use of private tutoring outside school hours does more harm than good, because it increases pressure on children and widens the gap between rich and poor families. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Mixed-age classrooms
questions.prompt: Some schools teach children of different ages together in the same class rather than grouping them strictly by year, so that older pupils help younger ones and each child progresses at their own pace. What are the advantages and disadvantages of mixed-age classrooms?

questions.subject: Student evaluations of teachers
questions.prompt: Some universities ask students to rate their lecturers, and use the results in decisions about promotion. Some people believe this makes teaching more accountable, while others argue that it rewards popularity rather than good teaching. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Four-day school week
questions.prompt: Some schools have reduced the school week to four longer days in order to save money and give pupils more time for rest and family life. To what extent do you agree or disagree that this is a positive change?

questions.subject: Overprotective parenting
questions.prompt: Many parents today closely supervise and manage almost every aspect of their children's lives, from their friendships to their schoolwork. What are the causes of this style of parenting, and what effects does it have on children as they grow up?

questions.subject: Qualities of a good teacher
questions.prompt: Teachers are often remembered long after their pupils have forgotten the details of what they were taught, for better or for worse. What qualities make a teacher truly effective, and to what extent can these qualities be developed through training?

questions.subject: Cost of childcare
questions.prompt: In many countries the cost of childcare has risen so high that some parents, particularly mothers, find it is not worth returning to work. What problems does this cause, and what solutions could governments and employers offer?

questions.subject: Equal parental leave for fathers
questions.prompt: In many countries mothers receive far more paid leave after the birth of a child than fathers do. Fathers should be entitled to the same length of paid parental leave as mothers, and should be encouraged to take all of it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Early specialisation in youth sport
questions.prompt: Children who show talent in a sport are increasingly encouraged to train intensively in that single sport from a very young age, often at the expense of other activities. What are the advantages and disadvantages of such early specialisation?

questions.subject: Selective schools for gifted pupils
questions.prompt: Some people believe that academically gifted children should be educated in separate schools where they can be stretched. Others argue that selective schools harm the children who are not chosen and divide communities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Shorter summer holidays
questions.prompt: The long summer holiday causes many children, especially those from poorer families, to forget much of what they learned during the year. It should therefore be replaced by shorter breaks spread more evenly throughout the year. How far do you agree?

questions.subject: Contract cheating at university
questions.prompt: An increasing number of university students pay others, often through online services, to complete their essays and assignments for them. What are the causes of this form of academic dishonesty, and what effects does it have on higher education?

questions.subject: Recorded lectures
questions.prompt: Many universities now record their lectures and make them available online, and attendance at lecture theatres has fallen as a result. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this practice for students and for the universities themselves?

questions.subject: Parental liability for youth crime
questions.prompt: When teenagers commit crimes, it is often argued that their upbringing is partly to blame. Parents should therefore be held legally responsible, and fined if necessary, when their children under eighteen break the law. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Persistent school absence
questions.prompt: In many schools the number of pupils who are regularly absent without good reason has risen significantly, and those pupils fall steadily behind their classmates. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could schools, parents and governments take to address it?

questions.subject: Handwriting versus typing
questions.prompt: Some educators believe that teaching handwriting is a waste of time now that most writing is done on keyboards. Others argue that learning to write by hand remains important for children's development. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Contextual university admissions
questions.prompt: Universities should lower their entry requirements for applicants from disadvantaged backgrounds, since grades achieved in under-resourced schools do not reflect those students' true potential. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this approach to admissions?

questions.subject: Steering students towards science
questions.prompt: Some people argue that governments should use funding and scholarships to steer more students into science, technology and engineering, where economies need skills. Others believe young people should be free to study whatever interests them. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Independence for young children
questions.prompt: Opinions differ widely about when children should be allowed to do things on their own, such as walking to school or using public transport. At what age should children be given this kind of independence, and what factors should parents consider?

questions.subject: Educational video games
questions.prompt: Some teachers now use video games in the classroom to teach subjects such as history, mathematics and science, arguing that pupils are more motivated when learning feels like play. What are the advantages and disadvantages of using games as a teaching tool?

questions.subject: Philosophy in primary school
questions.prompt: Philosophy, with its focus on reasoning, argument and questioning, is usually reserved for older students at university. It should instead be taught to children from the first years of primary school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Later school start times
questions.prompt: Research suggests that teenagers naturally fall asleep and wake later than adults. Some people therefore believe secondary schools should start later in the morning, while others argue this would disrupt families and fail to prepare students for working life. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Outdoor learning in schools
questions.prompt: Every school should require children to spend part of each week learning outdoors, in parks, gardens or woodland, rather than keeping all lessons inside the classroom. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Free lifelong adult education
questions.prompt: Governments should fund education for adults of all ages, so that people can retrain for a new career or study a new subject at any point in their lives without paying fees. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Copyright in AI-generated art
questions.prompt: Artificial intelligence can now produce paintings, music and poetry in seconds from a short text instruction. Some argue that such works should receive no copyright protection at all, because no human being truly created them. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: The right to be forgotten
questions.prompt: Some people believe individuals should have a legal right to have outdated or embarrassing information about them removed from search results. Others argue that this rewrites the public record and restricts freedom of expression. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Moving to a cashless society
questions.prompt: In a growing number of countries, cash is rapidly disappearing from shops and public transport as people pay for almost everything with cards and mobile phones. What are the advantages and disadvantages of moving towards a completely cashless society?

questions.subject: Banning anonymous online accounts
questions.prompt: Anonymous accounts allow people to abuse others online without consequences. For this reason, some argue that every social media user should be required to register under their real name. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Electronic waste from discarded devices
questions.prompt: Millions of tonnes of discarded phones, laptops and other electronic devices are thrown away every year, and much of this waste ends up in poorer countries. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to address it?

questions.subject: Decline of local newspapers
questions.prompt: In many regions, local newspapers have closed, leaving whole towns with no journalist reporting on their councils, courts and schools. What are the causes of this decline, and what effects does it have on local communities?

questions.subject: Regulating social media influencers
questions.prompt: Social media influencers are frequently paid to promote products to their followers without making this clear. Influencers should be regulated in exactly the same way as traditional advertisers. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Voice assistants in the home
questions.prompt: Voice-controlled assistants are now common in homes, answering questions, placing orders, playing music and controlling lights and heating, while listening constantly for a spoken command. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on these devices in everyday domestic life?

questions.subject: Breaking up large technology companies
questions.prompt: Some argue that a handful of technology companies have become so powerful that governments should break them into smaller businesses. Others believe their size allows them to offer better and cheaper services. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Responding to deepfake videos
questions.prompt: Technology now makes it possible to create convincing videos of people saying or doing things they never said or did. What dangers does this pose to society, and how should governments and individuals respond to it?

questions.subject: The right to repair devices
questions.prompt: Many electronic products are designed so that they cannot easily be repaired by their owners or by independent shops. Manufacturers should be legally required to make spare parts and repair manuals available to everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Cyberbullying among teenagers
questions.prompt: Online bullying has become a serious concern for teenagers, following them from the school gate into their homes through their phones. What are the main causes of this problem, and what can parents, schools and platforms do to reduce it?

questions.subject: Wearable health trackers
questions.prompt: Wearable devices now record their users' heart rate, sleep and physical activity around the clock, and some insurers offer discounts to those who share this data. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend?

questions.subject: Short-form video and attention spans
questions.prompt: Many teachers report that students find it increasingly difficult to concentrate on long texts or lectures, and some blame the popularity of very short online videos. What are the causes of declining attention spans, and what effects might this have?

questions.subject: News behind paywalls
questions.prompt: A growing number of newspapers now charge readers for access to their websites. High-quality journalism should be freely available to everyone, even if this means it must be funded in other ways. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Public funding of broadcasters
questions.prompt: Some people believe that a public broadcaster funded by taxpayers is essential for impartial news and educational programming. Others argue that in an age of countless online channels, such funding is no longer justified. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: AI in criminal sentencing
questions.prompt: Some courts are experimenting with computer programs that recommend sentences or predict whether an offender will reoffend. Decisions about a person's liberty should never be influenced by an algorithm. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Chatbots in customer service
questions.prompt: Many businesses now use automated chatbots rather than human staff to answer customer enquiries, handle complaints and process refunds at any hour of the day. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this development for companies and for their customers?

questions.subject: Rural broadband and the digital divide
questions.prompt: In many countries, people in rural areas still lack fast and reliable internet access, which limits their opportunities in education and employment. What are the causes of this digital divide, and what could be done to close it?

questions.subject: Banning targeted online advertising
questions.prompt: Online advertisers routinely track people's browsing history in order to show them personalised advertisements. This practice should be banned, and advertising should instead be based only on the content of the page being viewed. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Digital legacy after death
questions.prompt: Some people believe that the social media accounts, photographs and messages of people who have died should be preserved and passed on to their families. Others argue that they should be deleted, since the dead can no longer consent to how they are used. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Growth of online gambling
questions.prompt: Gambling through mobile phone apps and websites has grown rapidly in recent years, particularly among young men. What are the causes of this growth, and what effects is it having on individuals and their families?

questions.subject: Teaching students to evaluate online sources
questions.prompt: Young people now gather most of their information from the internet, where reliable and unreliable sources appear side by side. How can schools best teach students to judge the credibility of what they read online, and whose responsibility is this?

questions.subject: Banning autonomous weapons
questions.prompt: Military forces are developing weapons that can select and attack targets without direct human control. Such weapons should be banned by international law in the same way as chemical weapons. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Open-source software in government
questions.prompt: Governments spend large sums each year on software licences from private companies. All public services should be required to use open-source software, which anyone can inspect, modify and share. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Fake online reviews
questions.prompt: Consumers increasingly rely on online reviews when choosing products, restaurants and hotels, yet many of these reviews are fake or paid for. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?

questions.subject: Government access to encrypted messages
questions.prompt: Some argue that police and security services must be able to read encrypted messages in order to prevent crime and terrorism. Others believe that weakening encryption would put everyone's security and privacy at risk. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Publishing leaked documents
questions.prompt: Journalists sometimes publish confidential documents that have been leaked or stolen from governments and companies. The public interest in such information always outweighs the way in which it was obtained. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Online voting in elections
questions.prompt: Some countries are considering allowing citizens to vote in national elections over the internet rather than queuing in person at polling stations, arguing that this would make participation easier and raise turnout. What are the advantages and disadvantages of introducing online voting?

questions.subject: Young people aspiring to be influencers
questions.prompt: Surveys suggest that many children now say they want to become online influencers or video creators when they grow up, rather than doctors or engineers. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects might it have on society?

questions.subject: Platforms paying for news content
questions.prompt: Search engines and social media platforms display headlines and extracts from news articles without paying the organisations that produced them. These platforms should be required by law to pay news publishers for this content. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: AI companions and relationships
questions.prompt: Some people now form close emotional bonds with artificial intelligence programs designed to act as friends or partners. Some see this as a valuable source of comfort, while others fear it will weaken real human relationships. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Energy use of data centres
questions.prompt: The data centres that power the internet and artificial intelligence consume enormous amounts of electricity and water. What are the causes of this growing demand, and what measures could be taken to reduce its environmental impact?

questions.subject: Explainable algorithmic decisions
questions.prompt: Algorithms are increasingly used to decide who receives a loan, a job interview or a social benefit. Organisations should be legally required to explain in plain language how any such automated decision was made. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: In-game purchases in video games
questions.prompt: Many video games aimed at young players encourage them to spend real money on virtual items and random rewards. Should these features be treated as a form of gambling, and what responsibilities do game developers have towards their players?

questions.subject: Sensor-based smart cities
questions.prompt: Some cities are installing networks of sensors and cameras to manage traffic, energy use, waste collection and other public services automatically, often in partnership with private technology firms. What are the advantages and disadvantages of developing such smart cities?

questions.subject: Banning outdoor billboard advertising
questions.prompt: Billboards and digital advertising screens dominate the streets of most modern cities. Outdoor advertising should be banned from public spaces so that citizens are not exposed to commercial messages against their will. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: People avoiding the news
questions.prompt: A growing number of people say they deliberately avoid the news because they find it depressing or overwhelming. What are the causes of this behaviour, and what effects could it have on individuals and on democratic society?

questions.subject: Regulating new technology early
questions.prompt: Some argue that new technologies should be strictly regulated before they are widely adopted, in order to prevent harm. Others believe that early regulation stifles innovation and that rules should follow only once problems appear. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Online piracy of films and music
questions.prompt: Some people view downloading films and music without paying as theft that harms artists and creators. Others argue that piracy is mainly a response to high prices and limited availability, and that it sometimes introduces creators to new audiences. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Governments buying data from brokers
questions.prompt: Private companies collect and sell detailed information about people's locations, purchases and interests. Government agencies should be prohibited from buying this data, since they would need a warrant to collect it themselves. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: National digital identity systems
questions.prompt: Several governments are introducing digital identity systems that allow citizens to prove who they are, open bank accounts and access public services through a single online account linked to their personal records. What are the advantages and disadvantages of such systems?

questions.subject: Online activism and political engagement
questions.prompt: Some believe that social media has made young people more politically engaged by giving them an easy way to support causes. Others argue that sharing a post is no substitute for real political action. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Labelling edited advertising images
questions.prompt: Advertisements frequently use digitally altered images that make models appear thinner or more flawless than any real person. All such images should carry a clear label stating that they have been edited. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Renting rather than owning digital goods
questions.prompt: Increasingly, people pay monthly subscriptions for software, music, films and even car features rather than buying them outright. What are the causes of this shift from ownership to subscription, and what effects does it have on consumers?

questions.subject: Inaccessible websites for disabled users
questions.prompt: Many websites and apps remain difficult or impossible to use for people with visual, hearing or physical impairments. What are the causes of this problem, and what steps could governments and businesses take to address it?

questions.subject: Advertising of high-carbon products
questions.prompt: Tobacco advertising has been banned in many countries because of its harm to health. Advertisements for high-carbon products, such as flights and large petrol cars, should be banned for the same reason. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Crowdfunding platforms
questions.prompt: Online crowdfunding allows individuals to raise money directly from the public for inventions, creative projects and even urgent medical treatment, bypassing banks, publishers and other traditional gatekeepers. What are the advantages and disadvantages of raising money in this way?

questions.subject: AI-written news articles
questions.prompt: Some news organisations have begun using artificial intelligence to write reports on sport, finance and the weather. Some argue this frees journalists for deeper work, while others believe it will undermine the quality of journalism. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Robots caring for the elderly
questions.prompt: As populations age, some countries are developing robots to assist with the care of elderly people in their homes and in care facilities. Is this an acceptable solution to the shortage of carers, and what limits should be placed on it?

questions.subject: Police access to consumer DNA databases
questions.prompt: Millions of people have sent their DNA to private companies to learn about their ancestry. Police should be allowed to search these databases to identify suspects in serious crimes. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Online radicalisation of young people
questions.prompt: Young people are increasingly being drawn towards extremist views through online forums, recommended videos and gaming communities, often without their families noticing. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to prevent it?

questions.subject: Citizen journalism
questions.prompt: Ordinary people with smartphones are often the first to film and report on major events, long before professional journalists arrive, and their footage is shared worldwide within minutes. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on citizen journalism for news?

questions.subject: Internet access as a human right
questions.prompt: Access to the internet has become essential for education, work and participation in public life. It should therefore be recognised as a basic human right and provided free of charge by governments. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Press intrusion into private lives
questions.prompt: Newspapers and websites frequently report on the private lives of celebrities and politicians. The media should only publish such information when it is genuinely in the public interest. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Opt-out organ donation
questions.prompt: Some countries now presume that every adult has agreed to donate their organs after death unless they have formally registered an objection. Supporters say this saves lives, while critics say consent should never be assumed. To what extent do you agree or disagree that an opt-out system of organ donation should be adopted everywhere?

questions.subject: Compulsory childhood vaccination
questions.prompt: Some people believe that children should not be allowed to enrol in school unless they have received all recommended vaccinations. Others argue that parents must retain the right to make medical decisions for their own children. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Direct-to-consumer genetic testing
questions.prompt: Companies now sell genetic tests directly to the public, promising to reveal a customer's ancestry and risk of developing certain diseases. What are the advantages and disadvantages of making this kind of testing available without the involvement of a doctor?

questions.subject: Antibiotic resistance
questions.prompt: Many common infections are becoming harder to treat because bacteria have developed resistance to the antibiotics that once killed them. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken by doctors, farmers and governments to address it?

questions.subject: Paying blood donors
questions.prompt: In many countries blood is donated voluntarily and without payment, yet hospitals frequently report shortages. Some argue that offering donors money would solve the problem. To what extent do you agree or disagree that people should be paid for giving blood?

questions.subject: Rising short-sightedness in children
questions.prompt: Eye specialists report that short-sightedness among children has increased dramatically in recent decades, and in some East Asian cities most school leavers now need glasses. What are the causes of this rise, and what effects is it likely to have on individuals and on health services?

questions.subject: Paying for self-inflicted illness
questions.prompt: Illnesses linked to smoking, heavy drinking and poor diet place a considerable burden on public health services. Should people whose own choices have contributed to their illness be expected to pay more towards their treatment, and what problems might such a policy create?

questions.subject: Legalising assisted dying
questions.prompt: Some countries allow terminally ill adults to request medical assistance to end their lives, subject to strict safeguards. Opponents fear that vulnerable people could be pressured into this decision. To what extent do you agree or disagree that assisted dying should be legal?

questions.subject: Public funding for alternative medicine
questions.prompt: Some people believe that public health systems should pay for complementary treatments such as acupuncture and herbal remedies because many patients find them helpful. Others argue that only treatments proven by rigorous scientific evidence deserve public money. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Retirement villages
questions.prompt: In some countries, older people are increasingly moving into purpose-built retirement villages with their own shops, social activities and care on site. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this kind of housing for older people, their families and society?

questions.subject: Rural shortage of doctors
questions.prompt: In many countries, people living in rural and remote areas have far less access to doctors, nurses and hospitals than those in cities. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could governments take to ensure fairer access to healthcare?

questions.subject: Mental health lessons in schools
questions.prompt: Mental health education, covering topics such as managing stress and recognising the signs of illness, should be a compulsory subject in every secondary school. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Household food waste
questions.prompt: In wealthy countries, a large share of the food bought by households is thrown away without ever being eaten. What are the causes of this waste, and what effects does it have on the environment and the economy?

questions.subject: Plant-based diets
questions.prompt: Some people argue that everyone should adopt a mainly plant-based diet for the sake of their health and the planet. Others believe that meat and dairy remain an important part of a balanced diet and that eating habits are a personal matter. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Drug patents in poorer countries
questions.prompt: Many essential medicines remain unaffordable in low-income countries because they are protected by patents. Pharmaceutical companies should be required to give up these patents so that poorer countries can produce cheaper versions. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: Travelling abroad for medical treatment
questions.prompt: Growing numbers of patients travel abroad for operations and dental treatment that would cost far more, or involve long waiting lists, in their own country. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this medical tourism for the patients themselves and for the countries involved?

questions.subject: Online health misinformation
questions.prompt: False and misleading health advice spreads rapidly online, sometimes persuading people to avoid effective treatments or to try dangerous ones. Why has this become such a serious problem, and what practical steps could be taken to reduce its impact?

questions.subject: Energy drinks and minors
questions.prompt: High-caffeine energy drinks are widely consumed by teenagers, and some doctors have raised concerns about their effects on sleep, concentration and heart health. To what extent do you agree or disagree that the sale of these drinks to anyone under eighteen should be banned?

questions.subject: Research into extending lifespan
questions.prompt: Scientists are investigating ways to slow the ageing process and extend the human lifespan well beyond its current limits. Should public money be spent on this kind of research, and what consequences might a much longer lifespan have for society?

questions.subject: Cosmetic surgery
questions.prompt: Some people regard cosmetic surgery as a legitimate personal choice that can improve confidence and wellbeing. Others believe it is driven by unrealistic beauty standards and should be more tightly restricted, particularly for young people. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Widespread sleep deprivation
questions.prompt: Surveys suggest that many adults and teenagers regularly sleep far less than doctors recommend. What are the main causes of this lack of sleep, and what effects does it have on individuals and on society as a whole?

questions.subject: Genetically modified crops
questions.prompt: Genetically modified crops can be engineered to resist pests, survive drought or contain additional nutrients. However, many consumers remain suspicious of them. What are the advantages and disadvantages of growing and eating genetically modified food?

questions.subject: Universal free school meals
questions.prompt: Poor nutrition can affect a child's concentration, behaviour and long-term health. Every child in state education should therefore receive a free, nutritious lunch at school, regardless of their family's income. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Overcrowded hospital emergency departments
questions.prompt: Hospital emergency departments in many countries are overcrowded, with patients waiting many hours to be seen, often for conditions that are not emergencies at all. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to reduce the pressure on emergency care?

questions.subject: Decriminalising personal drug use
questions.prompt: Some people believe that the possession of illegal drugs for personal use should be treated as a health issue rather than a crime. Others argue that removing criminal penalties would encourage drug use and harm communities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Limiting doctors' shift lengths
questions.prompt: Junior doctors in many hospitals routinely work shifts of twelve hours or more. Some argue that the working hours of medical staff should be strictly limited by law to protect both doctors and patients. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Laboratory-grown meat
questions.prompt: Scientists are now able to grow meat from animal cells in a laboratory without raising and slaughtering livestock. What are the advantages and disadvantages of replacing conventional meat with meat produced in this way, for consumers, farmers and the environment?

questions.subject: Rising dementia rates
questions.prompt: The number of people living with dementia is expected to rise considerably in the coming decades. What are the reasons for this increase, and what effects will it have on families, health services and the wider economy?

questions.subject: Minimum pricing for alcohol
questions.prompt: Governments should set a minimum price for every unit of alcohol sold, in order to make cheap, strong drinks less affordable and reduce harmful drinking. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this policy?

questions.subject: Age in healthcare rationing
questions.prompt: Health services cannot afford to provide every expensive treatment to every patient who might benefit. Should a patient's age be taken into account when deciding who receives costly treatment, and what principles should guide such decisions?

questions.subject: Animal testing in medical research
questions.prompt: Some people believe that testing new medicines on animals is essential to protect human patients from harm. Others argue that it is cruel and that modern alternatives make it unnecessary. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Urban air pollution and illness
questions.prompt: Air pollution in large cities is linked to asthma, heart disease and other serious conditions, yet levels in many places remain high. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to protect public health?

questions.subject: Value of organic food
questions.prompt: Organic food is considerably more expensive than conventionally produced food, but it offers few real benefits to the health of the people who eat it. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

questions.subject: Artificial intelligence in diagnosis
questions.prompt: Computer systems trained on large numbers of medical images can now detect some diseases, including certain cancers, as accurately as experienced specialists. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on artificial intelligence to diagnose illness in hospitals and clinics?

questions.subject: Sedentary office work
questions.prompt: Many office employees spend most of their working day sitting at a desk, which is associated with a range of long-term health problems. Employers, rather than individuals, should be responsible for reducing the time their staff spend sitting. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Fluoridation of drinking water
questions.prompt: Adding fluoride to public drinking water is a cheap and effective way of preventing tooth decay, and it should be introduced wherever it is not already in use. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: National food self-sufficiency
questions.prompt: Some people believe that countries should aim to grow most of their own food in order to protect themselves against global shortages. Others argue that importing food from wherever it is produced most cheaply is more efficient. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Teenage eating disorders
questions.prompt: Eating disorders such as anorexia and bulimia are becoming more common among teenagers, and they often begin at an increasingly young age. What are the causes of this problem, and what can families, schools and the media do to tackle it?

questions.subject: Warning labels on processed food
questions.prompt: Ultra-processed foods, which contain many industrial additives, have been linked to a range of health problems. Some experts argue that they should carry health warnings similar to those printed on cigarette packets. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Weight-loss medication
questions.prompt: New prescription medicines can help people lose a significant amount of weight, and demand for them has grown rapidly. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on medication, rather than changes in diet and exercise, to tackle excess weight?

questions.subject: Mandatory health check-ups
questions.prompt: Every adult over the age of forty should be required to attend a free health check-up each year, so that conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure are detected early. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Preparing for healthy old age
questions.prompt: People in many countries are living longer, but not all of those extra years are spent in good health. What can individuals do during their working lives to ensure a healthy old age, and what role should governments play in supporting them?

questions.subject: Social prescribing
questions.prompt: Some doctors now refer patients with mild depression or anxiety to community activities such as gardening, art classes or walking groups rather than prescribing medication. Some see this as a sensible, humane approach, while others worry it delays proper treatment. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Decline of home cooking
questions.prompt: Fewer young people today know how to prepare a meal from basic ingredients, and many households rely heavily on ready meals and takeaways. What are the causes of this decline in cooking skills, and what effects is it having on health and family life?

questions.subject: Fast food outlets near schools
questions.prompt: Local authorities should refuse permission for new fast food outlets to open within walking distance of schools. To what extent do you agree or disagree that this is an effective way of improving children's diets?

questions.subject: Stigma around mental illness
questions.prompt: Many people who suffer from mental illness do not seek help because they fear being judged by their families, employers or communities. What are the causes of this stigma, and what measures could be taken to encourage people to seek treatment?

questions.subject: Pharmacists treating minor ailments
questions.prompt: In some countries, pharmacists are now allowed to diagnose and prescribe medicine for minor conditions such as ear infections and sore throats, without the patient seeing a doctor. What are the advantages and disadvantages of expanding the role of pharmacists in this way?

questions.subject: Generational tobacco ban
questions.prompt: Some governments have proposed permanently banning the sale of tobacco to anyone born after a certain year, so that a whole generation grows up unable to buy cigarettes legally. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this approach?

questions.subject: Electronic cigarettes and vaping
questions.prompt: Some people argue that electronic cigarettes are a valuable tool that helps smokers give up tobacco. Others believe that they are attracting a new generation of young people to nicotine addiction. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Sharing outbreak data internationally
questions.prompt: Infectious diseases can now cross the world within days because of international travel. Every country should therefore be legally obliged to report any new outbreak to international health authorities immediately, even at a cost to its economy. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Funding parity for mental health
questions.prompt: Mental health services should receive the same level of public funding as services for physical illness, since mental illness can be just as disabling. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: Vitamin and dietary supplements
questions.prompt: A large and growing number of people take vitamins, minerals and other dietary supplements every day, often without medical advice. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend for individuals and for public health?

questions.subject: Rising childhood allergies
questions.prompt: Food allergies and other allergic conditions appear to be far more common among children today than they were a few generations ago. What are the possible causes of this increase, and what effects does it have on children, their families and schools?

questions.subject: Retirement age and life expectancy
questions.prompt: As people live longer and remain healthy for more years, the age at which they can receive a state pension should rise in line with life expectancy. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Editing genes in human embryos
questions.prompt: Advances in genetic engineering may soon allow scientists to edit the genes of human embryos to prevent serious inherited diseases. Some welcome this as a medical breakthrough, while others fear it could lead to the creation of designer babies. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Phasing out zoos
questions.prompt: Some people argue that zoos are an outdated form of entertainment which confines intelligent animals for human amusement, and that they should be gradually closed. Others claim that zoos play a vital role in conservation and education. To what extent do you agree or disagree that zoos should be phased out?

questions.subject: Onshore wind farms in countryside
questions.prompt: Many governments are approving large onshore wind farms in rural areas, often close to villages and in open landscapes valued for their natural beauty. What are the advantages and disadvantages of generating electricity from wind farms in the countryside?

questions.subject: Soil degradation from intensive farming
questions.prompt: In many farming regions, fertile topsoil is being eroded and depleted far faster than it can naturally be replaced, threatening future harvests. What are the main causes of this soil degradation, and what measures could farmers and governments take to address it?

questions.subject: Carbon tax on fuel
questions.prompt: Some people believe that a tax on carbon, added to the price of petrol, gas and electricity, is the most effective way to cut emissions. Others argue that such a tax places an unfair burden on low-income households and rural workers. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Urban heat islands
questions.prompt: Large cities are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, particularly at night and during summer heatwaves. What are the causes of this urban heat island effect, and what effects does it have on the people who live in cities?

questions.subject: Tax on meat consumption
questions.prompt: Livestock farming is a significant source of greenhouse gases, and some experts have proposed a special tax on meat to reduce consumption. To what extent do you agree or disagree that governments should tax meat in order to protect the environment?

questions.subject: Pricing household water use
questions.prompt: In many countries, household water is supplied very cheaply or even free, regardless of how much is used. Should people pay a higher price for water in order to encourage conservation, and how could this be done fairly?

questions.subject: Robotic and automated farming
questions.prompt: Farms are increasingly using robots, drones and satellite data to plant, spray and harvest crops with very little human labour. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this automation of agriculture for farmers, rural communities and the natural environment?

questions.subject: Keeping pet cats indoors
questions.prompt: Domestic cats kill very large numbers of birds and small mammals every year, even when they are well fed at home. Owners should therefore be required by law to keep their cats indoors or within enclosed gardens. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Rewilding former farmland
questions.prompt: Some conservationists argue that large areas of farmland should be returned to nature, allowing forests, wetlands and wild animals to recover. Others believe that land is needed to produce food and support rural livelihoods. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Fast fashion textile waste
questions.prompt: Cheap clothing is now bought in huge quantities and often discarded after being worn only a few times, creating vast amounts of textile waste. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken by consumers, manufacturers and governments to solve it?

questions.subject: Banning short-haul flights
questions.prompt: Some countries have proposed banning domestic flights on routes where the same journey can be made by train in a few hours. To what extent do you agree or disagree that short-haul flights should be prohibited where a rail alternative exists?

questions.subject: Agricultural runoff polluting rivers
questions.prompt: Many rivers and lakes near farming areas now suffer from toxic algal blooms and declining fish populations. What are the causes of this form of water pollution, and what effects does it have on wildlife and on local communities?

questions.subject: Household rooftop solar panels
questions.prompt: Governments in several countries offer financial incentives to encourage homeowners to install solar panels on their roofs. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on households, rather than large power stations, to generate a share of a nation's electricity?

questions.subject: Banning private jets
questions.prompt: A single journey by private jet can produce more emissions than an average person generates in months. Some people therefore argue that private aviation should be banned or heavily restricted. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: Trophy hunting funding conservation
questions.prompt: Some people believe that allowing wealthy tourists to hunt wild animals for sport raises money that funds conservation and supports local communities. Others consider trophy hunting morally unacceptable in any circumstances. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Climate change in school curricula
questions.prompt: Climate change is expected to shape the lives of today's children more than those of any previous generation. Should it be taught as a compulsory subject in schools, and what should young people learn about it?

questions.subject: Artificial light pollution
questions.prompt: Artificial lighting in towns and cities has made the night sky almost invisible to many people and disrupts the behaviour of birds, insects and other wildlife. What are the causes of light pollution, and what practical measures could be taken to reduce it?

questions.subject: Ending fossil fuel subsidies
questions.prompt: Many governments continue to subsidise coal, oil and gas, keeping fuel prices low for consumers and industry. Some argue that all such subsidies should be abolished immediately to support the transition to clean energy. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Vertical farming in cities
questions.prompt: Vertical farms grow crops indoors in stacked layers under artificial light, often inside city buildings and without any soil. What are the advantages and disadvantages of producing food in this way compared with traditional farming in the countryside?

questions.subject: Climate-driven human displacement
questions.prompt: Increasing numbers of people are being forced to leave their homes because of droughts, floods and rising seas. What are the main causes of this climate-related displacement, and what effects is it likely to have on the regions that receive these people?

questions.subject: Insects as human food
questions.prompt: Some people argue that insects, which are rich in protein and need little land or water to farm, should become a normal part of the human diet. Others believe that most consumers will never accept them and that effort is better spent elsewhere. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Keeping exotic pets
questions.prompt: Reptiles, primates and other exotic animals are increasingly kept as household pets, often in conditions very different from their natural habitat. To what extent do you agree or disagree that the private ownership of exotic animals should be banned?

questions.subject: Flash flooding in cities
questions.prompt: Heavy rainfall now frequently overwhelms drainage systems in many cities, flooding streets, homes and transport networks. What are the causes of this increase in urban flooding, and what measures could city authorities take to reduce the damage it causes?

questions.subject: Ending sales of petrol cars
questions.prompt: Several governments have announced dates after which new petrol and diesel cars may no longer be sold, requiring buyers to choose electric vehicles instead. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this policy for consumers, industry and the environment?

questions.subject: Corporate carbon offsetting
questions.prompt: Many companies claim to be carbon neutral because they pay for trees to be planted or forests to be protected elsewhere, rather than reducing their own emissions. To what extent do you agree or disagree that carbon offsetting allows businesses to avoid real change?

questions.subject: Large hydroelectric dams
questions.prompt: Some argue that large hydroelectric dams provide clean and reliable electricity that developing countries urgently need. Others point out that they flood valleys, displace communities and destroy river ecosystems. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Supermarkets donating unsold food
questions.prompt: Supermarkets throw away large quantities of food that is still safe to eat. Some people believe that they should be legally required to donate all unsold edible food to charities. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Decline of pollinating insects
questions.prompt: Populations of bees, butterflies and other pollinating insects have fallen sharply in many parts of the world. What are the causes of this decline, and what effects could it have on food production and the natural environment?

questions.subject: Geoengineering to cool the planet
questions.prompt: Some scientists have proposed deliberately altering the Earth's climate, for example by reflecting sunlight back into space, in order to slow global warming. What are the potential advantages and disadvantages of relying on geoengineering to address climate change?

questions.subject: Intensive livestock farming conditions
questions.prompt: Much of the meat and eggs sold today comes from animals kept in crowded indoor conditions with little space to move. Some people argue that such intensive farming methods should be made illegal, even if food prices rise as a result. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Producer responsibility for electronic waste
questions.prompt: Discarded phones, computers and other electronic devices form one of the fastest growing types of waste. Some believe that manufacturers, rather than consumers or local councils, should be made responsible for collecting and recycling every device they sell. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Fracking for shale gas
questions.prompt: Some people argue that extracting gas from shale rock through hydraulic fracturing can improve energy security and lower prices. Others believe it risks contaminating water supplies and delays the move towards renewable energy. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Culling invasive species
questions.prompt: Invasive species introduced by humans, such as rats, foxes and certain fish, can devastate native wildlife. Some argue that large-scale culling of these animals is justified to protect vulnerable ecosystems. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this approach?

questions.subject: Legal rights for rivers
questions.prompt: In a few countries, natural features such as rivers and forests have been granted legal rights similar to those of a person, allowing cases to be brought on their behalf. Is this a sensible way to protect the natural environment, and what problems might it create?

questions.subject: Organic farming
questions.prompt: Organic farming avoids synthetic pesticides and fertilisers, and organic produce is increasingly popular with consumers despite its noticeably higher price. What are the advantages and disadvantages of organic farming for consumers, farmers and the wider environment?

questions.subject: Tropical rainforest clearance
questions.prompt: Vast areas of tropical rainforest continue to be cleared every year, despite international agreements to protect them. What are the main causes of this deforestation, and what effects does it have both locally and globally?

questions.subject: Deep-sea mining for battery metals
questions.prompt: Companies are preparing to mine the deep ocean floor for the metals needed in batteries for electric vehicles. Such mining should be prohibited until scientists understand far more about deep-sea ecosystems, even if this slows the switch to clean energy. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Human-wildlife conflict near farms
questions.prompt: As farms and settlements expand into natural habitats, conflicts between people and wild animals such as elephants, wolves and big cats are becoming more frequent. What are the causes of this problem, and what solutions would protect both communities and wildlife?

questions.subject: No-fishing marine reserves
questions.prompt: Some believe that large areas of the ocean should be declared marine reserves where all fishing is forbidden, allowing fish stocks to recover. Others argue that this threatens the livelihoods of coastal fishing communities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Public right to roam the countryside
questions.prompt: In some countries the public may walk freely across most private countryside, while in others much of the land is closed to them. Everyone should have a legal right to walk on uncultivated private land, provided they respect it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Seawater desalination plants
questions.prompt: Desalination plants, which remove salt from seawater to make it drinkable, are increasingly being built in dry coastal regions where rainfall is unreliable. What are the advantages and disadvantages of depending on desalination to supply a population with fresh water?

questions.subject: Small farms versus industrial agriculture
questions.prompt: Some people believe that small family farms should be protected by governments because they sustain rural communities and traditional practices. Others argue that only large, industrial farms can produce enough affordable food for a growing population. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Animals in entertainment
questions.prompt: Animals are still used in circuses, rodeos, marine parks and races to entertain paying audiences, often travelling long distances between shows. To what extent do you agree or disagree that the use of animals for public entertainment should be banned?

questions.subject: Eco-anxiety among young people
questions.prompt: Many young people report feelings of fear and hopelessness about the future of the planet, a condition sometimes described as eco-anxiety. Why do you think this is becoming more common, and how should parents, schools and governments respond?

questions.subject: Replacing gas boilers with heat pumps
questions.prompt: Some argue that governments should require households to replace gas boilers with electric heat pumps in order to reduce emissions from home heating. Others believe the high cost of installation makes this unfair unless it is entirely voluntary. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: De-extinction of lost species
questions.prompt: Advances in genetic science may soon make it possible to bring back animals that have become extinct. Some argue that this money would be far better spent protecting species that still survive. To what extent do you agree or disagree that attempts at de-extinction should be pursued?

questions.subject: Desertification of drylands
questions.prompt: In many dry regions, once productive land is gradually turning into desert, leaving farmers and herders unable to make a living. What are the causes of this desertification, and what measures could be taken to prevent it and restore damaged land?

questions.subject: Biofuels made from crops
questions.prompt: Fuels made from crops such as maize, sugar cane and palm oil are widely promoted as a renewable alternative to petrol and diesel. What are the advantages and disadvantages of using farmland to grow crops for fuel rather than for food?

questions.subject: Increasing severity of wildfires
questions.prompt: Wildfires are becoming larger, more frequent and more destructive in many parts of the world, including regions that rarely experienced them in the past. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on people, economies and ecosystems?
