questions.subject: Zero-carbon standards for new buildings
questions.prompt: Buildings account for a large share of energy use through heating, cooling and lighting. Some argue that every new building should be legally required to produce no net carbon emissions, even if this makes construction more expensive. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Stray animal population control
questions.prompt: Some people believe that stray dogs and cats which cannot be rehomed should be humanely put down to control their numbers. Others argue that every animal shelter should adopt a policy of never destroying healthy animals. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Sea-level rise in coastal cities
questions.prompt: Rising sea levels threaten many of the world's largest coastal cities with flooding, erosion and the contamination of drinking water. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could governments take to protect coastal populations?

questions.subject: Mass tree-planting schemes
questions.prompt: Governments and companies increasingly promote schemes to plant millions of trees as a solution to climate change. Some critics argue that such schemes are a distraction from the harder task of cutting emissions. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: Paying farmers for environmental stewardship
questions.prompt: Agricultural subsidies have traditionally rewarded farmers for how much food they produce. Some argue that farmers should instead be paid mainly for protecting soil, water and wildlife on their land. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Gig worker employment rights
questions.prompt: People who find work through delivery and ride-hailing apps are usually classed as self-employed, which means they receive no sick pay, holiday pay or pension. Such workers should be given the same legal protections as ordinary employees. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Job hopping versus company loyalty
questions.prompt: Some people believe that changing employer every two or three years is the fastest way to build skills and raise one's salary. Others argue that staying with one organisation for many years brings greater security, trust and long-term reward. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Early access to pension savings
questions.prompt: Some governments now allow people to withdraw money from their retirement savings years early, for example to buy a first home or to cope with a period of hardship. What are the advantages and disadvantages of allowing early access to pension savings in this way?

questions.subject: Banning unpaid internships
questions.prompt: Unpaid internships give an unfair advantage to young people whose families can support them, while excluding talented applicants from poorer backgrounds. For this reason, they should be made illegal. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: Late payment of small suppliers
questions.prompt: Small businesses frequently wait months to be paid by the large companies they supply, and some are forced to close even though their order books are full. What are the causes of this problem of late payment, and what measures could governments and industry take to solve it?

questions.subject: Buy now pay later debt
questions.prompt: Online retailers increasingly offer services that allow shoppers to split a purchase into instalments and pay later, and many young consumers now rely on them. What are the causes of the popularity of these schemes, and what effects are they having on personal finances?

questions.subject: Abolishing mandatory retirement age
questions.prompt: No employer should be allowed to force a worker to retire simply because they have reached a certain age. Decisions about when to stop working should be based on ability and personal choice alone. How far do you agree with this statement?

questions.subject: Raising the minimum wage
questions.prompt: Some argue that a substantial rise in the minimum wage is the most effective way to reduce poverty among working families. Others warn that it will lead businesses to cut jobs and raise prices. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Self-employment as a career
questions.prompt: A growing number of people are choosing to work for themselves as freelancers or sole traders rather than as employees of an organisation. What are the advantages and disadvantages of self-employment compared with a conventional salaried job?

questions.subject: Renting versus buying a home
questions.prompt: In many countries owning a home is seen as a sign of success, yet a growing number of people now rent for their whole lives. Is buying a home still a wise financial goal, and what should people consider before deciding whether to rent or to buy?

questions.subject: Capping executive pay ratios
questions.prompt: The gap between the pay of senior executives and that of ordinary employees has grown enormously in many large firms. Governments should set a legal limit on how many times more a chief executive may earn than the lowest-paid worker. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Explaining the gender pay gap
questions.prompt: Some people believe that the gender pay gap is mainly the result of discrimination by employers and should be tackled through stricter laws. Others argue that it largely reflects differences in the careers and working hours that men and women choose. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Taxing fast fashion
questions.prompt: Cheap clothing that is worn only a few times before being thrown away causes serious environmental and social harm. Governments should therefore impose a special tax on low-cost, disposable fashion. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Open-plan offices
questions.prompt: Many organisations have replaced private offices and cubicles with large open-plan workspaces in which staff sit together without walls or partitions. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this type of office design for employees and employers?

questions.subject: Passion versus salary
questions.prompt: Some people believe that young people should choose a career they are passionate about, even if it pays poorly. Others argue that financial security should come first and that personal interests can be pursued outside work. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Planned obsolescence in products
questions.prompt: Many consumers complain that phones, appliances and other electronic goods now break or become outdated far sooner than they used to. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on consumers and the environment?

questions.subject: Corporate duty beyond profit
questions.prompt: The only responsibility of a business is to make a profit for its owners, and social or environmental goals should be left to governments and charities. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

questions.subject: Skilled trades shortage
questions.prompt: Many countries are facing a serious shortage of electricians, plumbers, builders and other skilled tradespeople, while fewer young people are choosing these careers. What are the causes of this problem, and what could be done to solve it?

questions.subject: Regulating cryptocurrency speculation
questions.prompt: Digital currencies are too volatile and too easily used for fraud to be left unregulated. Governments should strictly control, or even ban, their purchase by ordinary investors. How far do you agree with this view?

questions.subject: Measuring success beyond GDP
questions.prompt: Some economists argue that gross domestic product remains the best measure of a nation's progress. Others believe that governments should instead judge success by indicators such as health, happiness and environmental quality. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Performance-related pay
questions.prompt: Many employers now link a significant part of their staff's pay to individual performance targets, rather than paying everyone in the same role a fixed salary. What are the advantages and disadvantages of performance-related pay for employees and organisations?

questions.subject: Tipping in service industries
questions.prompt: In some countries, workers in restaurants, hotels and taxis depend heavily on tips from customers to earn a living wage. Is tipping a fair way to reward service workers, or should it be replaced by higher fixed wages?

questions.subject: Taxing luxury goods
questions.prompt: Luxury items such as designer handbags, sports cars and private yachts should be taxed at a much higher rate than everyday goods, and the revenue should be used to support public services. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Rising cost of living
questions.prompt: In recent years, households in many countries have seen the prices of food, energy and rent rise faster than their incomes. What are the causes of this rising cost of living, and what effects is it having on individuals and society?

questions.subject: Offshoring manufacturing
questions.prompt: Over recent decades, many companies in wealthy countries have moved their manufacturing to nations where labour and production costs are much lower. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this practice for both the wealthy and the developing countries involved?

questions.subject: Relevance of trade unions
questions.prompt: Trade unions played an important role in improving working conditions in the past, but they are no longer necessary in a modern economy where employment law already protects workers. How far do you agree with this statement?

questions.subject: Saving versus spending when young
questions.prompt: Some people believe that young adults should save as much of their income as possible to secure their future. Others argue that youth is the time to spend money on travel and experiences that cannot be repeated later. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Brain drain from developing countries
questions.prompt: Many highly qualified doctors, engineers and scientists leave developing countries to work in wealthier nations, where salaries and conditions are better. What problems does this cause for their home countries, and what measures could be taken to address it?

questions.subject: Restricting weekend trading hours
questions.prompt: Shops and shopping centres should be required to close on one day every week so that workers and families can spend time together away from commerce. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this idea?

questions.subject: Rise of second jobs
questions.prompt: An increasing number of people now hold a second job or run a small business alongside their main employment. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on workers and their families?

questions.subject: Retail loyalty schemes
questions.prompt: Most large retailers now offer loyalty cards and apps that reward customers with discounts in exchange for data about everything they buy. What are the advantages and disadvantages of these loyalty schemes for shoppers and for the businesses that run them?

questions.subject: Gambling advertising
questions.prompt: Advertising for gambling, including sports betting and lottery products, encourages addiction and leads many households into financial hardship. It should therefore be banned from television, websites and sporting events altogether. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Degree requirements for jobs
questions.prompt: Some employers insist that applicants hold a university degree, even for roles that do not obviously require one. Others believe that hiring should be based on demonstrated skills and experience rather than formal qualifications. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Employers cutting staff training
questions.prompt: Many employers now spend little on training their staff, preferring to recruit people who already have the skills they need. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could governments and businesses take to encourage greater investment in workplace training?

questions.subject: Banning zero-hours contracts
questions.prompt: Zero-hours contracts allow employers to call on staff only when they are needed, without guaranteeing any fixed hours or income. Such contracts should be banned, so that every employee is guaranteed a minimum number of paid hours each week. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Supporting new start-ups
questions.prompt: A large proportion of new businesses close within their first few years of trading, often leaving their founders in debt. Why do so many start-ups fail, and what support, if any, should governments provide to new entrepreneurs?

questions.subject: AI screening of job applicants
questions.prompt: Many large employers now use artificial intelligence software to sort job applications and decide which candidates should be invited for an interview, often before any human has read them. What are the advantages and disadvantages of recruiting in this way?

questions.subject: Growing wealth inequality
questions.prompt: In many countries, the gap between the richest and poorest members of society has widened considerably over recent decades. What are the causes of this growing inequality, and what effects does it have on society?

questions.subject: Higher inheritance tax
questions.prompt: Wealth passed from one generation to the next should be taxed much more heavily, because inherited fortunes give some people an advantage they have done nothing to earn. How far do you agree with this view?

questions.subject: Government bailouts of companies
questions.prompt: When large companies face collapse, some believe governments should rescue them with public money to protect jobs and the wider economy. Others argue that failing businesses should be allowed to close. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Counterfeit goods
questions.prompt: The trade in counterfeit products, ranging from fake clothing and watches to imitation medicines and spare parts, continues to grow worldwide. What problems does this trade create for consumers and legitimate businesses, and what measures could be taken to reduce it?

questions.subject: Employee monitoring software
questions.prompt: Employers are entitled to use software that records their employees' keystrokes, screens and working hours, since staff are paid for the time they spend at work and should expect it to be checked. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Global brands in developing markets
questions.prompt: International restaurant chains and retail brands are opening branches in more and more developing countries, often competing directly with small local traders. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this expansion for local economies and communities?

questions.subject: Ethical boycotts by consumers
questions.prompt: Consumers have a moral duty to avoid buying products made in factories where workers are poorly paid or treated unsafely, even if this means paying considerably more or buying less. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Responsibility for retirement pensions
questions.prompt: Some people believe that individuals should be responsible for saving enough money for their own retirement. Others argue that the state should guarantee every older citizen an adequate pension. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Compulsive consumer spending
questions.prompt: Many people today buy far more goods than they need, often on impulse, and homes are filling with items that are rarely used. What are the causes of this behaviour, and what are its effects on individuals and society?

questions.subject: Charging shoppers for online returns
questions.prompt: Many online shoppers order several items and send most of them back, and free returns create large amounts of packaging, transport and waste. Online retailers should therefore charge customers for every item they return. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Workplace bullying
questions.prompt: Bullying and harassment at work remain common in many organisations, and victims are often reluctant to report it. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to create safer workplaces?

questions.subject: Teaching leadership skills
questions.prompt: Organisations spend large sums of money training their staff to become managers and leaders. What qualities make someone an effective manager, and can these qualities be taught through training, or are they largely a matter of personality?

questions.subject: Single global currency
questions.prompt: The world economy would be more stable, and international trade and travel would be far easier, if every country abandoned its national currency and used one shared global currency. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this idea?

questions.subject: Privatising public services
questions.prompt: Many governments have transferred services such as railways, water supply and postal delivery from public ownership to private companies that run them for profit. What are the advantages and disadvantages of privatising public services in this way?

questions.subject: Mandatory product sustainability labels
questions.prompt: All products sold in shops should carry a clear label showing their environmental impact, such as the carbon emissions produced in making and transporting them, so that consumers can make informed choices. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Large corporations versus small firms
questions.prompt: Some people believe that starting a career in a large corporation offers the best training and prospects. Others think that working for a small company provides wider experience and greater responsibility. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Informal cash economy
questions.prompt: In many countries, a significant amount of work is paid in cash and never declared to the tax authorities. What are the causes of this problem, and what can governments do to bring this activity into the formal economy?

questions.subject: Price rises during emergencies
questions.prompt: Businesses that sharply raise the prices of essential goods such as bottled water, fuel or medicine during natural disasters and other emergencies are exploiting people in distress, and they should face criminal penalties. How far do you agree with this view?

questions.subject: Green belt development
questions.prompt: Many cities are surrounded by protected green belts on which building is forbidden. Some planners argue that this land should now be released for new housing, since the need for homes outweighs the value of the countryside it protects. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: High-rise versus low-rise density
questions.prompt: Some urban planners believe that growing cities should build upwards, housing people in tall apartment towers. Others argue that dense low-rise neighbourhoods of terraced houses and small blocks create healthier and more sociable communities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Short-term holiday rentals
questions.prompt: Online platforms now allow homeowners to rent out flats and houses to tourists for a few nights at a time, often in ordinary residential streets. What are the advantages and disadvantages of short-term holiday rentals for local residents and for the cities concerned?

questions.subject: Rough sleeping and homelessness
questions.prompt: The number of people sleeping on the streets has increased in many wealthy cities, even as those cities have grown richer. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could governments and communities take to address it?

questions.subject: Fare-free public transport
questions.prompt: Fares on buses, trams and trains are a significant cost for many city residents, particularly those on low incomes. Some argue that public transport in cities should therefore be completely free to use, funded through general taxation rather than ticket sales. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Gentrification of neighbourhoods
questions.prompt: In many cities, traditionally working-class neighbourhoods are being transformed as wealthier residents, cafes and expensive shops move in. What are the causes of this process of gentrification, and what effects does it have on the people who already live there?

questions.subject: Measuring city liveability
questions.prompt: International rankings regularly claim to identify the most liveable cities in the world. What do you think makes a city a good place to live, and are such rankings a reliable guide for people deciding where to settle?

questions.subject: Compulsory cycle helmets
questions.prompt: Cyclists who ride without a helmet risk serious head injuries in even minor accidents. Wearing a helmet should therefore be compulsory for every cyclist, including adults, and those caught without one should be fined. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Rent controls
questions.prompt: Some people argue that governments should cap how much landlords can raise rents each year in order to protect tenants. Others believe that rent controls discourage investment and eventually reduce the supply of rental homes. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Relocating government departments
questions.prompt: Some governments are moving ministries and public agencies out of the capital to smaller cities in poorer regions, taking thousands of civil service jobs with them. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relocating government departments in this way, for the staff involved and for the regions concerned?

questions.subject: Tourist taxes
questions.prompt: Popular destinations often struggle to pay for the extra rubbish collection, policing and maintenance that visitors require. Every tourist who stays overnight in such a place should therefore pay a nightly tax, with the money spent on local services and infrastructure. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Loss of rural services
questions.prompt: Banks, post offices, shops and bus routes are closing in many small villages, leaving residents with few essential services nearby. What are the causes of this problem, and what practical steps could be taken to keep rural communities viable?

questions.subject: Reallocating road space to cyclists
questions.prompt: Cycling in many cities remains dangerous because riders must share busy roads with cars and lorries. City authorities should take space away from motor vehicles on main roads and give it to protected cycle lanes, even if this makes driving slower. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Tree planting and urban heat
questions.prompt: As summers grow hotter, cities are becoming dangerously warm compared with the surrounding countryside. Planting trees on a large scale is the most effective way to keep cities cool. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

questions.subject: Skills-based immigration selection
questions.prompt: Some believe that countries should admit immigrants mainly according to their qualifications and the skills the economy needs. Others argue that family ties and humanitarian need should carry equal weight. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Ride-hailing apps and taxis
questions.prompt: Smartphone apps now allow passengers to summon a private driver within minutes, and in many cities they have taken much of the business once held by licensed taxis. What are the advantages and disadvantages of ride-hailing apps for passengers, drivers and the cities in which they operate?

questions.subject: Taxing empty homes
questions.prompt: Owners who leave residential properties empty for long periods should be heavily taxed, or even required to rent them out, while so many people need somewhere to live. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Urban noise pollution
questions.prompt: Noise from traffic, construction, aircraft and nightlife is now recognised as a serious threat to the health of city dwellers. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to reduce it?

questions.subject: Capping visitors at heritage sites
questions.prompt: Famous historic sites such as ancient temples and old city centres are being damaged by the sheer number of people who visit them each day. The number of visitors to such places should be strictly capped, even if this means many people are unable to see them. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Global population and resources
questions.prompt: The world's population is expected to continue rising for several decades before it levels off. Is population growth the main threat to the planet's natural resources, or is the level of consumption in wealthy countries the more serious problem? Give reasons for your answer.

questions.subject: Remote workers moving to the countryside
questions.prompt: Since remote work became common, many professionals have left large cities to live in rural towns and villages, bringing city salaries with them. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this movement for the rural communities that receive these newcomers?

questions.subject: Volunteer tourism
questions.prompt: Some people believe that volunteer tourism, in which travellers pay to work on projects in developing countries, genuinely helps local communities. Others argue that it mainly benefits the volunteers and can even cause harm. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Growth of single-person households
questions.prompt: In many countries a rising proportion of adults now live alone, and single-person households have become one of the most common types of home. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on individuals, on the housing market and on society?

questions.subject: Second homes in coastal villages
questions.prompt: In popular coastal and rural villages, many houses now stand empty for most of the year as holiday homes, while local families cannot afford to buy. The purchase of second homes should therefore be banned in such places. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Litter and illegal dumping in cities
questions.prompt: Litter, discarded furniture and illegally dumped rubbish are a common sight in the streets and parks of many cities. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could local authorities and residents take to keep public spaces clean?

questions.subject: Protecting urban parks
questions.prompt: As land in cities becomes more valuable, local authorities are often tempted to sell parks and playing fields to developers. Public green spaces in cities should never be sold or built on, however high the price offered for the land. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

questions.subject: Fuel taxes and rural drivers
questions.prompt: Some argue that high taxes on petrol and diesel are necessary to reduce emissions. Others point out that such taxes fall hardest on rural residents, who have no alternative to driving. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Building new towns from scratch
questions.prompt: Some governments are building entirely new towns on open land to house their growing populations, rather than expanding the cities that already exist. What are the advantages and disadvantages of creating new towns in this way, for the people who move there and for the country as a whole?

questions.subject: Citizenship language tests
questions.prompt: Many countries now expect people applying for citizenship to demonstrate knowledge of the national language. Some argue that immigrants should be required to pass a demanding language test before they are granted citizenship of their new country. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Designing cities for older residents
questions.prompt: The proportion of older people living in cities is rising quickly in many countries. How should cities be designed to meet the needs of an ageing population, and who should pay for the changes that are needed?

questions.subject: Money sent home by migrants
questions.prompt: Migrants working abroad send billions of dollars home to their families every year, and in some countries these payments are worth more than all the foreign aid they receive. What are the causes of this growth in remittances, and what effects does it have on the countries that receive them?

questions.subject: Hosting major sporting events
questions.prompt: Cities often compete fiercely for the right to host major international sporting events such as the Olympic Games. What are the advantages and disadvantages of hosting such an event for the city and its residents?

questions.subject: Halting airport expansion
questions.prompt: Air travel is one of the fastest-growing sources of greenhouse gas emissions, and many airports are planning new runways and terminals. No further expansion of airports should be permitted, since growth in flying is incompatible with efforts to limit climate change. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Historic buildings versus redevelopment
questions.prompt: Some people believe that old buildings in city centres should be preserved at almost any cost. Others argue that cities must be free to replace them with modern structures that better meet present needs. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Substandard rental housing
questions.prompt: Many tenants live in rented homes that are damp, poorly insulated or in need of urgent repair, yet feel unable to complain. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to improve the condition of rental housing?

questions.subject: Foreign buyers of property
questions.prompt: In some cities, a large share of new apartments is bought by overseas investors who never live in them. Foreign buyers who do not intend to reside in a country should be prohibited from purchasing residential property there. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Seasonal migrant farm labour
questions.prompt: Many farming regions depend on temporary workers from abroad to plant and harvest crops each season before returning home. What are the advantages and disadvantages of seasonal labour schemes of this kind for the workers themselves, for the farmers and for the host country?

questions.subject: Growth of informal settlements
questions.prompt: In many developing countries, informal settlements without proper sanitation or legal tenure are expanding rapidly on the edges of large cities. What are the causes of this growth, and what effects does it have on residents and on the city as a whole?

questions.subject: Tourism in fragile environments
questions.prompt: Some believe that tourists should be allowed to visit fragile natural environments such as polar regions and coral reefs, since this builds support for their protection. Others argue that these places should be closed to visitors altogether. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Government-built social housing
questions.prompt: Rising demand for affordable homes has not been met by private developers in many countries. Governments should build large numbers of homes directly and let them at low rents, rather than relying on the private market to meet housing need. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Refugee employment barriers
questions.prompt: Many refugees hold qualifications and professional experience, yet end up unemployed or in jobs far below their skill level. What are the causes of this problem, and what could governments and employers do to solve it?

questions.subject: Retesting older drivers
questions.prompt: Older drivers are sometimes involved in accidents caused by declining eyesight or slower reactions, yet in many countries a licence lasts for life. Drivers over the age of seventy should be required to retake their driving test every few years. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Multigenerational households
questions.prompt: In some countries, it is increasingly common for grandparents, parents and adult children to live together under one roof, often for financial reasons. What are the advantages and disadvantages of multigenerational living for the different members of the families involved?

questions.subject: Closing small village schools
questions.prompt: Some people believe that village schools with very few pupils should be closed and merged into larger schools in nearby towns in order to save money. Others argue that the village school is the heart of a rural community and must be kept open. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Urban sprawl
questions.prompt: Many cities are spreading outwards into low-density suburbs that stretch far into the surrounding countryside. What are the causes of this urban sprawl, and what effects does it have on the environment and on the people who live there?

questions.subject: Lower residential speed limits
questions.prompt: Research suggests that pedestrians are far more likely to survive a collision with a slower vehicle. The speed limit on all residential streets should therefore be reduced to 30 kilometres per hour, even though this will lengthen many journeys. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Ageing farming workforce
questions.prompt: In many countries, the average age of farmers is rising steadily because few young people are willing to take up agriculture. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could ensure that there are enough farmers in the future?

questions.subject: Gated communities
questions.prompt: Some people believe that gated residential communities offer families safety and a strong sense of neighbourhood. Others argue that they divide cities along lines of wealth and weaken public life. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: The night-time economy
questions.prompt: Some cities are encouraging bars, restaurants, shops, gyms and public transport to operate through the night, creating a twenty-four hour economy. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this development for businesses, workers and the residents who live nearby?

questions.subject: Indigenous control of tourism
questions.prompt: Indigenous and traditional communities should have the final say over whether tourists may visit their land, and should receive a substantial share of the income that tourism generates. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Limiting megacity growth
questions.prompt: Some of the world's cities now contain more than twenty million people. Should governments try to limit the growth of their largest cities, and what could they do to encourage people to live in smaller regional centres instead?

questions.subject: Adult children living with parents
questions.prompt: An increasing number of young adults in their late twenties and thirties continue to live in their parents' home. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on young people and their families?

questions.subject: Moving freight from road to rail
questions.prompt: Some argue that governments should shift the transport of goods from lorries to railways to reduce emissions and road damage. Others believe that rail freight is too slow and inflexible for a modern economy. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Local veto over development
questions.prompt: Proposals for new housing, roads or wind farms often meet strong opposition from the people who live closest to them. Local residents should have the right to block any development planned near their homes. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this principle?

questions.subject: Cruise ships in historic ports
questions.prompt: Large cruise ships should be banned from docking in small historic ports, since the crowds they bring in a few hours overwhelm the town while contributing little to the local economy. How far do you agree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Public funding of political parties
questions.prompt: Political parties in many countries depend on large donations from wealthy individuals and companies. Private donations to parties should be banned altogether, with election campaigns funded instead from public money in proportion to each party's support. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Parental monitoring of teenagers
questions.prompt: Some parents believe they should be able to monitor their teenage children's messages, location and online activity in order to keep them safe. Others argue that such monitoring damages trust and prevents young people from developing independence. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Trial by jury
questions.prompt: In many legal systems, serious criminal cases are decided by a jury of ordinary citizens rather than by professional judges. What are the advantages and disadvantages of leaving verdicts in the hands of people with no legal training?

questions.subject: Gender quotas on company boards
questions.prompt: Several governments now require large companies to ensure that a minimum proportion of their board members are women. Supporters see this as the fastest route to equality, while opponents argue that appointments should be based on merit alone. To what extent do you agree or disagree with mandatory gender quotas for company boards?

questions.subject: Knife crime among young people
questions.prompt: In a number of cities, the carrying of knives by teenagers and young adults has become a serious concern, leading to injuries and deaths. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken by communities and authorities to reduce it?

questions.subject: Rising divorce rates
questions.prompt: Divorce rates have risen considerably in many parts of the world over the past half century. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on children, families and society as a whole?

questions.subject: Mandatory minimum sentences
questions.prompt: Some legal systems impose mandatory minimum sentences for certain crimes, removing the judge's discretion to give a lighter punishment. Supporters say this ensures consistency and deters offenders. To what extent do you agree or disagree that mandatory minimum sentences are a fair and effective approach to justice?

questions.subject: Referendums on national decisions
questions.prompt: Instead of leaving major decisions to elected representatives, some governments ask the whole population to vote directly on important issues through a referendum. What are the advantages and disadvantages of deciding complex national questions in this way?

questions.subject: Allowing the sale of kidneys
questions.prompt: Some people argue that adults should be allowed to sell one of their kidneys, since a regulated market would save the lives of patients waiting for transplants. Others believe it would exploit the poor and turn the human body into a commodity. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Compulsory community service for students
questions.prompt: Some schools require students to complete a set number of hours of unpaid community service before they can graduate. Is making volunteering compulsory a good way to develop responsible citizens, and what other methods could encourage young people to contribute to their communities?

questions.subject: Zero alcohol limit for drivers
questions.prompt: In many countries people may legally drive after drinking a small amount of alcohol. The legal limit should be reduced to zero, so that any trace of alcohol in a driver's blood is a criminal offence. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Parental versus professional childcare
questions.prompt: Some people believe that young children are best raised at home by a parent during their first years of life. Others argue that high quality professional childcare benefits children and allows both parents to continue working. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Boys falling behind girls at school
questions.prompt: In many countries boys now leave school with lower grades than girls and are less likely to go on to university. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could schools, families and governments take to address it?

questions.subject: Term limits for legislators
questions.prompt: Some people argue that members of parliament and other elected legislators should be limited to serving a fixed number of terms, in order to bring fresh ideas into politics and prevent the abuse of power. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Legalised and taxed gambling
questions.prompt: Many governments have legalised gambling, including online betting, and now collect substantial tax revenue from it while regulating the industry. What are the advantages and disadvantages of legalising and regulating gambling rather than prohibiting it, both for individuals and for society as a whole?

questions.subject: Increase in shoplifting
questions.prompt: Retailers in many cities report a sharp increase in shoplifting, with some stores locking up everyday goods or closing altogether. What are the causes of this rise in shop theft, and what effects is it having on businesses and local communities?

questions.subject: Legal duty to help strangers in danger
questions.prompt: In some countries it is a criminal offence to ignore a person in serious danger, for example by failing to call an ambulance, when help could be given safely. Every country should adopt such a law. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Age of criminal responsibility
questions.prompt: The age at which children can be prosecuted for a crime varies widely between countries. Some believe it should be raised so that young offenders are dealt with outside the courts, while others argue that children who commit serious crimes must be held accountable. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Adopted people tracing birth parents
questions.prompt: In some countries, people who were adopted as babies have no legal right to discover who their birth parents are. Adopted adults should always be entitled to this information, even if the birth parents would prefer to remain anonymous. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Citizens' assemblies
questions.prompt: Some governments have begun to form citizens' assemblies, in which randomly selected members of the public study a policy issue and make recommendations. What are the advantages and disadvantages of involving ordinary citizens in policymaking in this way?

questions.subject: Underreporting of domestic abuse
questions.prompt: Domestic abuse is widely believed to be one of the most underreported crimes, with many victims never contacting the police or seeking help. Why do so many cases go unreported, and what could be done to support victims in coming forward?

questions.subject: Philanthropy by the very wealthy
questions.prompt: Some of the richest individuals in the world donate large sums to causes of their own choosing, such as health, education and scientific research. Is private philanthropy an adequate substitute for public spending funded by taxation, and should the wealthy have this much influence over social priorities?

questions.subject: Publicly funded legal aid
questions.prompt: Access to a lawyer is essential for justice, yet legal fees place representation beyond the reach of many ordinary people. To what extent do you agree or disagree that governments should provide free legal representation to anyone who cannot afford it, including in civil disputes?

questions.subject: Decline of community organisations
questions.prompt: Membership of clubs, charities, trade unions and other community organisations has fallen steadily in many countries. What are the causes of this decline in civic participation, and what effects is it likely to have on society?

questions.subject: Routinely armed police
questions.prompt: In some countries police officers carry firearms at all times, while in others most officers are unarmed. Some believe that routinely armed police are necessary to protect the public, while others argue that they increase the risk of violence. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Restrictions on former officials lobbying
questions.prompt: Senior politicians and civil servants often take well paid jobs with private companies soon after leaving office. Some argue that former officials should be banned from lobbying their previous departments for several years. To what extent do you agree or disagree with such a restriction?

questions.subject: Growing up as an only child
questions.prompt: In many countries, families with a single child are becoming increasingly common, often because of the cost of raising children or because parents start later. What are the advantages and disadvantages of growing up as an only child rather than with brothers and sisters?

questions.subject: Women in frontline combat roles
questions.prompt: Several countries now allow women to serve in frontline combat units in the armed forces, while others still restrict them to support positions. Every military role, including combat, should be open to women on exactly the same terms as men. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Street harassment of women
questions.prompt: Surveys in many cities suggest that a large proportion of women experience harassment in streets and on public transport, and many change their routines as a result. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to make public spaces safer for everyone?

questions.subject: Giving money to people begging
questions.prompt: Some people believe that giving money directly to people begging in the street is a simple act of kindness. Others argue that it can do more harm than good, and that donations should go to charities which provide support services instead. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Declining marriage rates
questions.prompt: Fewer people are getting married than in previous generations, and many couples now choose to live together without marrying. What are the reasons for this change, and what effects might it have on families and society?

questions.subject: Expunging old criminal records
questions.prompt: Some argue that minor criminal convictions should be removed from a person's record after a period without reoffending, so that employers cannot see them. Others believe employers have a right to know. To what extent do you agree or disagree that old criminal records should be erased?

questions.subject: Private security replacing police
questions.prompt: In many cities, shopping centres, residential estates and even public streets are increasingly patrolled by private security companies rather than by the police. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on private security to maintain public order?

questions.subject: Freedom of information laws
questions.prompt: Freedom of information laws give citizens the right to request documents held by government bodies. How important is this right to a healthy democracy, and what information, if any, should governments be allowed to keep secret?

questions.subject: Legal protection for whistleblowers
questions.prompt: Employees who reveal wrongdoing within their organisations often lose their jobs or face legal action for breaking confidentiality. To what extent do you agree or disagree that whistleblowers should receive full legal protection, even when they disclose confidential information?

questions.subject: Hate speech laws
questions.prompt: Some believe that laws against hate speech are necessary to protect minority groups from abuse and discrimination. Others argue that such laws threaten freedom of expression and give authorities too much power to decide what may be said. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Human trafficking
questions.prompt: Human trafficking, in which people are moved across or within borders and forced into labour or exploitation, remains widespread despite international efforts to stop it. What factors allow this crime to continue, and what could governments and businesses do to combat it more effectively?

questions.subject: Grandparents' right to see grandchildren
questions.prompt: When parents separate or fall out with their own families, grandparents are sometimes prevented from seeing their grandchildren. Grandparents should have a legal right to stay in contact with their grandchildren, whatever the parents' wishes. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Televising court proceedings
questions.prompt: Some countries now allow cameras into courtrooms so that trials can be broadcast on television or streamed online. What are the advantages and disadvantages of televising court proceedings for the justice system and the public?

questions.subject: Underrepresentation of women in politics
questions.prompt: Although women make up around half of the population, they remain a minority in most national parliaments and governments. What are the causes of this underrepresentation, and what effects does it have on political decision making?

questions.subject: Strike bans for essential workers
questions.prompt: Strikes by workers in essential public services, such as hospitals, fire services and public transport, can put lives at risk and disrupt entire cities. Some therefore argue that these workers should not be permitted to strike at all. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Sharing a family surname after marriage
questions.prompt: Some people believe that when a couple marries, one partner should take the other's surname so that the whole family shares a single name. Others think both partners should keep their own names, arguing that the tradition reflects outdated ideas. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Dual citizenship
questions.prompt: An increasing number of countries allow their citizens to hold the nationality of another country at the same time. What are the advantages and disadvantages of dual citizenship for individuals and for the nations involved?

questions.subject: Scams targeting older people
questions.prompt: Older people are increasingly targeted by telephone and doorstep fraudsters who pose as banks, officials or tradesmen, and many lose their life savings. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could families, banks and governments take to protect them?

questions.subject: Victims' role in sentencing
questions.prompt: In some courts, victims of crime are invited to describe how an offence has affected them before the judge decides on a sentence. To what extent do you agree or disagree that victims should have a direct influence on the punishment an offender receives?

questions.subject: Wrongful convictions
questions.prompt: Every year, a number of people are found to have been imprisoned for crimes they did not commit, sometimes after many years. What are the main causes of wrongful convictions, and what effects do they have on the individuals concerned and on public confidence in the justice system?

questions.subject: Devolving power to local government
questions.prompt: Some people argue that decisions about services such as transport, housing and policing should be made by local councils rather than by national government. Others believe that central control ensures fairness and consistency across the whole country. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: A duty to give a tenth of income
questions.prompt: People who live in wealthy countries have a moral obligation to give a significant share of their income, such as a tenth, to charities helping the poorest people in the world. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: Plea bargaining
questions.prompt: In many legal systems, defendants are offered a reduced sentence in exchange for pleading guilty, which avoids the need for a full trial. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this practice of plea bargaining?

questions.subject: Child poverty in wealthy nations
questions.prompt: Even in some of the world's richest countries, a significant proportion of children grow up in households that cannot afford adequate food, heating or housing. What are the causes of child poverty in wealthy nations, and what steps could governments take to reduce it?

questions.subject: Gender-neutral official language
questions.prompt: Some governments and public institutions have begun replacing gendered job titles and pronouns in official documents with gender-neutral alternatives. Why have they chosen to make this change, and should such language be required in all public communication, or left as a matter of choice?

questions.subject: Compulsory first-aid training
questions.prompt: Many people would not know what to do if someone collapsed in front of them in the street. Every adult should therefore be required to complete basic first-aid training, and to renew it every few years. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Commercial surrogacy
questions.prompt: Some argue that women should be allowed to be paid for carrying a pregnancy on behalf of another couple, as this helps people who cannot have children. Others believe commercial surrogacy exploits women and treats children as products. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Lifetime bans for corrupt officials
questions.prompt: Public officials who are convicted of corruption, such as accepting bribes or misusing public funds, should be banned from holding any public office for the rest of their lives. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Income-based fines
questions.prompt: In most countries, a fine for an offence such as speeding is the same amount for everyone, which means it barely affects the wealthy. Some argue that fines should instead be calculated as a proportion of the offender's income. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this approach?

questions.subject: Removing statues of controversial figures
questions.prompt: Many cities contain public statues of historical figures whose actions are now widely condemned. Some people argue that these statues should be removed from public squares and placed in museums, where they can be explained in context. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Athletes speaking out on politics
questions.prompt: Some people believe that professional athletes should use their fame to speak out on political and social issues. Others argue that sport should remain separate from politics and that athletes should confine themselves to competing. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Machine translation replacing language learning
questions.prompt: Machine translation software has become accurate enough that many people now rely on it instead of learning a foreign language. What are the advantages and disadvantages of depending on this technology for communication between speakers of different languages?

questions.subject: Value of citizen science
questions.prompt: Amateur volunteers now contribute to research by counting birds, monitoring rivers or classifying galaxies online. Some argue that such citizen science is just as valuable as the work of professional researchers and deserves far more funding. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Disappearance of minority languages
questions.prompt: Linguists warn that a large proportion of the world's languages may disappear within this century, as younger generations stop speaking the languages of their parents. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to protect endangered languages?

questions.subject: Growth of solo travel
questions.prompt: More and more people, including many older adults, are choosing to go on holiday entirely on their own rather than with family or friends. What are the causes of this growing trend towards solo travel, and what effects does it have on travellers and on the tourism industry?

questions.subject: Legalising performance-enhancing drugs
questions.prompt: Despite strict testing, the use of performance-enhancing drugs remains common in professional sport. Some commentators suggest that these substances should be permitted under medical supervision, since a ban cannot be enforced effectively. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

questions.subject: Subsidising traditional crafts
questions.prompt: Some believe governments should subsidise traditional crafts such as weaving, pottery and woodcarving so that these skills are not lost. Others argue that crafts which cannot survive commercially should be allowed to disappear. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Open access to publicly funded research
questions.prompt: Much scientific research is paid for by taxpayers, yet the results are often published in journals that charge high fees to read them. Should the findings of publicly funded research be freely available to everyone, and who should bear the cost of publishing them?

questions.subject: Video technology in refereeing
questions.prompt: Many sports now use video replay technology to help referees and umpires make difficult decisions during matches, and some fans argue that it slows the game down. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on this technology in professional sport?

questions.subject: Graffiti as legitimate art
questions.prompt: Graffiti and street art are often treated as vandalism and removed at public expense. However, some people argue that they are a legitimate art form that brings colour and meaning to urban spaces. To what extent do you agree or disagree that street art should be protected rather than removed?

questions.subject: Public distrust of scientific experts
questions.prompt: In many societies, a significant number of people now distrust the advice of scientists on issues such as vaccination and diet, preferring information from unofficial sources. What are the causes of this problem, and what could be done to rebuild public confidence in science?

questions.subject: Children abandoning organised sport
questions.prompt: Research in several countries suggests that many children give up organised sport in their early teenage years and never return to it. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on young people and on society as a whole?

questions.subject: Restricting commercial space tourism
questions.prompt: Private companies now offer short flights into space to wealthy customers, and the industry is expected to grow. Given the fuel consumed and the emissions produced, some argue that space tourism should be heavily restricted or banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Separating art from the artist
questions.prompt: Some people believe that the work of artists, writers and musicians who have behaved badly in their private lives should no longer be displayed, performed or taught. Others argue that a work of art should be judged separately from the person who made it. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: World Heritage Site status
questions.prompt: Many towns and natural landscapes compete to be officially recognised as sites of world heritage importance. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this status for the local communities who live in and around these places?

questions.subject: Correcting regional dialects in schools
questions.prompt: Some educators believe that schools should teach every child the standard form of the national language and actively discourage the use of regional dialects in the classroom. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this approach?

questions.subject: Abusive behaviour by sports spectators
questions.prompt: Violence, racist chanting and online abuse directed at players and referees remain common among sports fans in many countries. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could clubs, governing bodies and governments take to address it?

questions.subject: Women underrepresented in engineering
questions.prompt: Although more women than ever attend university, they remain underrepresented in fields such as engineering, physics and computer science. What are the causes of this imbalance, and what effects does it have on these professions and on society?

questions.subject: Scientists' responsibility for their discoveries
questions.prompt: Scientific discoveries can be used to cure diseases or to build weapons. Some people argue that scientists bear moral responsibility for how their discoveries are eventually used, and should refuse to work on research that may cause harm. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Esports as a recognised sport
questions.prompt: Competitive video gaming now attracts millions of spectators and offers large prizes to professional players. Should esports be recognised as a sport in the same way as football or athletics, and what would be gained or lost by doing so?

questions.subject: Free entry to national museums
questions.prompt: Some people believe that national museums and galleries should be free for everyone to enter, since their collections belong to the public. Others argue that visitors should pay an entrance fee so that museums can maintain their buildings and collections. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Artificial intelligence doing scientific research
questions.prompt: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly used to design new drugs, predict the structure of proteins and even propose scientific hypotheses for researchers to test. What are the advantages and disadvantages of relying on artificial intelligence to carry out scientific research?

questions.subject: Rebuilding destroyed monuments exactly
questions.prompt: When historic monuments are destroyed by war, fire or natural disaster, some people insist they should be rebuilt exactly as they were. Others feel that the ruins, or a new design, would be a more honest response. To what extent do you agree that destroyed monuments should be faithfully reconstructed?

questions.subject: Libraries becoming community hubs
questions.prompt: Many public libraries are reducing their collections of printed books in order to offer computers, workshops, events and meeting spaces instead. What are the advantages and disadvantages of transforming libraries into community centres of this kind?

questions.subject: Banning dangerous combat sports
questions.prompt: Combat sports such as boxing can cause serious and permanent injuries, including brain damage, to those who take part. Some people believe these sports should be banned altogether, while others see this as an unacceptable limit on personal freedom. To what extent do you agree that dangerous combat sports should be banned?

questions.subject: Closure of local live music venues
questions.prompt: In many towns and cities, small live music venues and local theatres are closing down at an increasing rate. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects is it likely to have on communities and on the next generation of performers?

questions.subject: Curiosity-driven versus applied research
questions.prompt: Some people argue that scientists should be free to pursue research driven purely by curiosity, since many great discoveries were made this way. Others believe research funding should be directed towards solving practical problems such as disease and hunger. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Virtual reality museum exhibits
questions.prompt: Museums increasingly use digital screens, virtual reality and interactive displays alongside, or even in place of, original objects, in an effort to attract younger audiences. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this approach for museums and their visitors?

questions.subject: Texting harming written language
questions.prompt: Some teachers claim that the abbreviations and informal style used in text messages and social media are damaging young people's ability to write correctly and formally. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

questions.subject: Ownership of space mining resources
questions.prompt: Several countries and private companies are planning to extract minerals from the Moon and from asteroids. Who should have the right to own and profit from resources found in space, and how should such activity be regulated?

questions.subject: Fraud and misconduct in research
questions.prompt: Cases of scientific fraud, in which researchers falsify data or copy the work of others, are being uncovered with growing frequency. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could universities and journals take to prevent it?

questions.subject: Public funding for Olympic medals
questions.prompt: Many governments spend large sums of public money training elite athletes in the hope of winning Olympic medals. Some argue that this money would be better spent encouraging ordinary citizens to exercise. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Structured activities versus free play
questions.prompt: Some parents fill their children's free time with organised activities such as music lessons, sports clubs and tutoring. Others believe children benefit more from unstructured time to play and explore on their own. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Accumulation of orbital space debris
questions.prompt: The number of satellites and fragments of debris orbiting the Earth has increased dramatically in recent decades. What are the causes of this build-up of space debris, and what effects could it have on future space activity and on life on Earth?

questions.subject: Holidaying at home instead of abroad
questions.prompt: Instead of travelling overseas, many families now spend their holidays in their own country, or stay at home and make day trips to nearby places. What are the advantages and disadvantages of holidaying close to home rather than going abroad?

questions.subject: Historical accuracy in films
questions.prompt: Films and television dramas based on real historical events often change facts to create a more entertaining story. Some people believe that producers have a duty to represent history accurately, because audiences may accept what they see as true. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Looting of archaeological sites
questions.prompt: Archaeological sites in many parts of the world are being looted, and the objects removed are sold to private collectors through an international black market. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to protect these sites?

questions.subject: Protecting languages from loanwords
questions.prompt: Some people believe that official bodies should protect their national language from foreign loanwords, particularly those borrowed from English. Others argue that languages have always evolved by borrowing, and that such efforts are pointless. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Statistical literacy for all citizens
questions.prompt: Modern public debates about health, the economy and the environment are full of statistics that many people struggle to interpret. Some argue that a basic understanding of statistics is now essential for every citizen in a democracy. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Foreign ownership of sports clubs
questions.prompt: A growing number of professional sports clubs are being bought by foreign investors and wealthy overseas owners. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend for the clubs, their supporters and the sport as a whole?

questions.subject: Revival of vinyl records and film cameras
questions.prompt: Vinyl records, film cameras and printed photographs have become fashionable again among young people who grew up with digital technology. What are the causes of this revival of older formats, and what effects is it having on consumers and on the industries concerned?

questions.subject: Broadcasting signals to alien civilisations
questions.prompt: Some scientists propose sending deliberate radio messages into space in the hope of contacting intelligent life elsewhere in the universe. Others warn that revealing our existence could be dangerous. To what extent do you agree that humanity should not attempt to broadcast its presence to other civilisations?

questions.subject: Borrowing from other cultures in art
questions.prompt: Artists, designers and musicians frequently borrow styles, symbols and traditions from cultures other than their own. When is it acceptable to draw on another culture in creative work, and at what point does it become disrespectful?

questions.subject: Match-fixing and illegal betting
questions.prompt: Match-fixing, in which players or officials deliberately influence the result of a game for gambling profits, has been uncovered in many sports. What are the causes of this problem, and what steps could be taken to protect the integrity of sport?

questions.subject: Using medical records without consent
questions.prompt: Anonymised medical records could help researchers discover the causes of many diseases. Some argue that such data should be available for research without asking each patient's permission, because the public benefit outweighs the risk to privacy. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Traditions involving animal cruelty
questions.prompt: Some traditional festivals and customs involve practices that cause harm to animals. Some people argue that these events are an important part of cultural heritage and should be preserved. Others believe that cruelty cannot be justified by tradition. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: International megascience collaborations
questions.prompt: Many of the largest scientific projects, such as particle accelerators and space telescopes, are now built and run by partnerships of many countries. What are the advantages and disadvantages of conducting scientific research through such large international collaborations?

questions.subject: Using leisure time to learn skills
questions.prompt: Some people believe that adults should use their leisure time productively, by learning new skills or studying, rather than simply relaxing or watching entertainment. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view of how free time should be spent?

questions.subject: University teaching in English
questions.prompt: Universities in many non-English-speaking countries now teach a growing number of courses in English in order to attract international students. Universities should teach mainly in the national language, even if this makes them less attractive to students from abroad. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

questions.subject: Major sporting events on free television
questions.prompt: Some people believe that major national sporting events, such as cup finals and international tournaments, should be shown only on free television so that everyone can watch. Others argue that sport needs the income earned by selling exclusive rights to subscription channels. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Musicians unable to earn a living
questions.prompt: Although more music is being listened to than ever before, many musicians and songwriters say they can no longer earn a living from their recordings. What are the causes of this problem, and what could be done to ensure that artists are paid fairly?

questions.subject: Scientists explaining work to the public
questions.prompt: Some people believe that every scientist who receives public funding should be required to explain their work to the general public, through talks, articles or school visits. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this requirement?

questions.subject: Compulsory musical instrument learning
questions.prompt: Some people believe every child should be required to learn a musical instrument at school, because music develops discipline and creativity. Others argue that it should remain optional, as not all children have the interest or aptitude. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

questions.subject: Traditional cuisine as protected heritage
questions.prompt: National heritage is usually associated with monuments, buildings and works of art. However, some argue that traditional cuisine and methods of cooking are just as important to a nation's identity and deserve the same official protection. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
